Boot: zero RAM files 1..7 (CALL reuses the clear-file subroutine above).
Boot: run two init subroutines, then enter the interpreter.

column2: OR handler (opcode A): Rd <- Rd OR Rs (bitwise). Shares the register write-back tail at 15:2f.
RUN CHECK (reached each interpreter pass): if the "execute this pass" flag M(0,8).3 is set, run one instruction (08:02); else service the keypad (1e:1a).
(padding: 0x00 bytes to end of page)
Operand fetch helpers: resolve a register operand (file 7 = user registers R0..RF) into A / scratch.
EXECUTE-INSTRUCTION entry: advance the program counter, then fetch the next instruction from external SRAM.

column1: # ---- Page 17: operand resolution & register write-back (chapter 1, page 7) ----

column2: Operand data path: resolve source/immediate operands into A, write results back to the destination register. Home of MOV / MOVI.

OPCODE DISPATCH. Decode command digit M(1,2) via an ACxAC (add-const, test-carry) ladder that catches F,E,...,5 in turn; 0-4 fall through to the second-level table on page 11. Each arm is an LDP p / BR off to that opcode's handler.
Second-level opcode dispatch: commands 0-4 (11:00), and the F-group decoded by its second digit (11:17 -> pages 18/19/1a, or 12:00 for F0-F8).
Control flow: GOTO/CALL set the program counter; BRC/BRZ test the flags in M(4,13) and, if set, branch by reusing GOTO. CALL saves the return address in M(1,13):M(1,14) (RET restores it).
SUB/SUBI/CMP/CMPI: SAMAN computes Rd - operand; CARRY = "no borrow" (M(4,13).0), ZERO if the result is 0 (M(4,13).1). CMP/CMPI discard the difference; SUB/SUBI store it to Rd.
Shared helper 1a:00 = "A <- Rd". The rest of the page implements SHR (F9d) and SHL (FAd).

EXTERNAL 2114 SRAM READ. Fetches one 3-nibble instruction into M(1,2):M(1,1):M(1,0). Address = {M(1,5):M(1,4) high bits, R5:R4 nibble-select}; R11=KL routes the L data lines onto K; each nibble is TKA'd and bit-inverted (09:23). Data is stored complemented in SRAM.
Helper: one's-complement a nibble (used to invert SRAM data on read; also a general NOT).
EXTERNAL 2114 SRAM WRITE (mirror of the 09:02 read): address via 0b:20, the 3 data nibbles driven onto R7..R10, each latched by an R13 write strobe. Used by keypad program entry and the PGM loaders.

7-SEGMENT DISPLAY REFRESH. Multiplexes the six digits: for each, TDO drives the segments (the hardware OPLA decodes the nibble to a 7-seg pattern) and SETR strobes that digit's common line (R0..R5); a short delay holds it lit, then RSTR moves to the next. SL into TDO = the decimal point (CARRY / ZERO / 1Hz flag dots).
